cards.text: Right before this, the prophet prayed for the LORD to tear open the heavens and come down, and he asked whether the LORD would keep silent (Isaiah 64:1, 12). Now the LORD speaks. And He starts with people who never asked for Him and never even looked for Him.

cards.question: The LORD talks about people who never asked for Him and never looked for Him. What does He do for them?

answers.text: He waits for them to ask first

cards.text: To a nation that didn't even call His name, He says, 'Here I am! Here I am!' Friend, after all my years in that junk drawer, I'd have CRIED if anybody said that to me just ONCE.
All day long, the LORD says, He has held out His hands to an obstinate people who walk in the wrong path. ALL DAY, friend. My mustache gives out holding a cookie tray for ten minutes.

cards.question: The LORD holds out His hands all day to these people. What does He say they follow?

cards.text: And the LORD says these people provoke Him continually. Not behind His back, friend. Right to His face.

cards.question: These people keep provoking the LORD. Where are they offering their sacrifices?

cards.text: It keeps going. They sit among the graves and spend nights in secret places, and I did years in a dark drawer and NEVER once volunteered for it.

cards.question: Along with polluted broth from their bowls, these people are eating the meat of ___.

cards.text: Then they tell people, 'Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!' That's a baker covered head to toe in flour telling YOU to go wash up.

cards.question: The LORD hears people saying they're holier than everyone else. What does He say people like that are to Him?
The LORD says it is written before Him, and after all these people have done, He will keep silent.

cards.text: No silence here. The LORD says He will repay, and He'll pay it back right into their laps.

cards.question: The LORD says He will repay their iniquities and also the iniquities of their ___.

cards.text: And He names it plainly. They burned incense on the mountains and scorned Him on the hills.

cards.question: For their former deeds, the LORD says He will measure only part of the payment into their laps.

cards.text: Then the LORD paints a picture. When new wine is found in a cluster of grapes, men say, 'Do not destroy it, for it contains a blessing.'

cards.question: Like that cluster with a blessing in it, what does the LORD say He'll do for His servants?

cards.text: Nobody throws out the cluster with the blessing in it. Friend, Mother Miller pulled me out of a closing bakery's bin for a QUARTER, so I know exactly how it feels when somebody decides you're worth keeping.
The LORD says He'll bring forth descendants from Jacob and heirs from Judah. HEIRS, friend! The only thing I ever inherited was a 25-cent price sticker.

cards.question: The LORD says His elect will possess His mountains, and His servants will dwell there.

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about the land. Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds.

cards.question: Sharon and the Valley of Achor will be for the LORD's people who ___ Him.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns back to the ones who forsake Him and forget His holy mountain. Friend, I lose my timer under a pile of dough, but a whole MOUNTAIN?

cards.question: Who does the LORD say these people are setting a table for?

cards.text: They fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny. And the LORD says, 'I will destine you for the sword, and you will all kneel down to be slaughtered.'

cards.question: Why does the LORD say the sword is coming for the ones who forsook Him?

answers.text: He called and they did not answer
They forgot to bring an offering

cards.text: Therefore the Lord GOD lays it out side by side: His servants on one side, the ones who forsook Him on the other. Same oven, friend, two VERY different batches.

cards.question: The Lord GOD says His servants will go hungry while the ones who forsook Him will eat.
The Lord GOD says His servants will rejoice. What happens to the ones who forsook Him?

answers.text: They will be put to shame

cards.text: His servants will shout for joy with a glad heart, the kind of LOUD that would wake up my whole bakery. The others will cry out with a heavy heart and wail with a broken spirit.

cards.question: The ones who forsook the LORD will leave behind their ___ as a curse for His chosen ones.
The Lord GOD will give His servants another name.

cards.text: Whoever invokes a blessing or takes an oath in the land will do it by the God of truth. Not like the expired coupon I shared that drawer with, swearing up and down it was STILL GOOD.

cards.question: Blessings and oaths in the land will be by the God of truth, for the former troubles will be ___ and hidden from His sight.

findings.problem: Isaiah 65:8 opens a comparison with "As the new wine is found in a cluster of grapes... so I will act on behalf of My servants." The card changes "As" to "When", so the simile becomes an event.
The question says "Like that cluster with a blessing in it". "That cluster" points back to story card 1, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card adds nothing new from the passage. "Nobody throws out the cluster with the blessing in it" restates Isaiah 65:8, which cards 1 and 2 already covered, and then the card adds a joke. It works as a recap card and does not move the passage forward.
The joke depends on Mother Miller and the closing bakery's bin. Neither was set up earlier in this lesson, and onboarding only establishes the junk drawer. The card never says who Mother Miller is.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: Jacob and Judah appear here for the first time in the lesson. The card does not say simply who they are.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question asks who "these people" are setting a table for. It never says who these people are (the ones who forsake the LORD and forget His holy mountain), so it relies on story card 8, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The statement says "after all these people have done" without saying who these people are or what they did. It relies on earlier cards the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The opening card tells facts from Isaiah 64:1 and 64:12, from the passage before this one, and gives their references inline in the text. Its verses field only cites Isaiah 65:1. Citing "from the first verse it uses to the last" would mean Isaiah 64:1-65:1, which pulls in verses 64:2-11 that the card never uses.
findings.question: When a story card uses context verses from outside the passage and gives their references inline, should its verses field include them, and how should non-consecutive context verses be cited? Or does the verses field cover only the passage verses it tells?
